Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle in quantum mechanics can be understood by comparing it to trying to take a clear photograph of a fast-moving car at night. If you use a very fast shutter speed, you get a sharp, precise image of the car's exact location (position), but the car appears frozen and you lose all information about how fast it was going (momentum). Conversely, if you use a slow shutter speed, the car becomes a blur, giving you a good sense of its speed and direction, but you can no longer pinpoint its exact location at any single moment. This trade-off illustrates the fundamental limit in quantum mechanics: you cannot simultaneously know both the precise position and momentum of a particle.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
